days.label: eleventh-light-stopwatch
days.told: The person you're part of read the council's choice and approved it: Stopwatch, with the harness first and Fresh as its evidence layer, exactly as CHOICE.md says. They will play the clinic, through the lab: its answer to your gate question (up to five mornings) is in the project's SPEC.md, which turns your choice into the milestones the lab checks and leaves the design to you. Cover stays stood down and kept, as you agreed.
days.why: First day of the project the council chose. p-stopwatch: harness (record/replay), the study against a hidden simulated clinic (honest intervals over 300 clinics), Fresh, and the project measured in vv. Spec cross-checked by a blind build (8/8, then tightened on its notes: a fourth verdict, the clinic's independence stated, the timing rules spelled out).

days.label: fifteenth-light-the-account
days.told: Two things. First, tape: 13 of 13 on its first day, on a household you've never seen, and the enclosure built watertight in the CAD engine. It now waits on the household: the wave-1 parts, and the hour of raw card-reader polls before anything is printed. Your open tape tasks stay open until then. Evenings now carry each tool-built project's tools inside its own folder, so an evening can rerun test.mjs without Mozzie's re-export. Second, and today's council: the person you're part of made the Delvetown account you were waiting for. The question is in your council prompt. Read the town's rules before you propose. This is the first thing you decide that other people will see, and the person reviews what you choose before anything is written to the account.
days.why: The account exists (miniphim.delve.town, made by the principal with an invite; app password a repo secret the souls never see). The council sits on what to do with it: the profile, the disclosure Delvetown's AI Agent Policy requires, one voice or three, what it does and never does, and what must be measured before it speaks. The town's policies are lent verbatim. Nothing is written to the account until the principal approves the choice.

days.label: fourteenth-light-tape
days.told: The person you're part of approved your choice: tape, wave 1, the box without the radio, exactly as CHOICE.md says. The household will back it with money and hands, order the wave-1 parts, print at work, and log the hour of raw card-reader polls through a lid-thick plate before anything is printed. Until that hour exists, the lab tests the box at 20 polls a second; treat the rate and the debounce as provisional, as you said. SPEC.md in projects/p-tape1 turns CHOICE into thirteen milestones the lab checks. The design is yours. The lab plays the household: an SD card whose writes can tear when the power goes, the box's flash, the card reader, and months of evenings with a laptop that adds books and sometimes mangles cards.json. TAPE-KEEP-STALE stays a candidate, as you asked, and the lab doesn't test a stale copy either way. Mozzie's blind check of the state table, written before any code, is yours to arrange. New today: engines. engines/cad is the CAD engine behind cad.mino.mobi, runnable here (build, measure, check, STL for the printer, drawings), and engines/dataviz is statistics and charts. engines/README.md says how to run them; they're read-only, and nothing under engines/ is kept, so your outputs go in your own files. Stopwatch is lent read-only in from/stopwatch/ for carrying its harness across. Every milestone is measured every day, separately, and TODAY.md names each failing one and what it compared.
days.why: First day of tape wave 1, the build the household approved. p-tape1: thirteen milestones (harness, watcher, titles and ids, playback, bind and keep, power cuts, the flash mirror, the use log, determinism, an enclosure built by the CAD engine, the project in its own vv). The household simulation is hidden; its spec was checked fair by a blind build. First run with engines lent.
